entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE. The taxonomy ranks a gain of a splice site as more amenable than weakened exon definition, because a cryptic site can often be blocked by an ASO whereas rescuing a weakened exon needs silencer blocking.
entries.snippet: a gain of a splice site is more amenable to rescue than a weakening of exon definition, because repressing a cryptic splice site can often be achieved by simply blocking the site with an ASO, whereas promoting a weakened exon requires identifying and blocking silencer elements within or near the exon.

entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE. Figure 2 as an image: a variant with severe damage to canonical splicing or coding function is routed to the unlikely amenable class, while no or little damage with gain of a site is the probably amenable class; this is the authors own prediction taxonomy.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2: arrow labelled Severe leads to Unlikely amenable; No to little damage with Gain leads to Probably amenable; Moderate damage with Gain or skipping or retention leads to Possibly amenable.

entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE. Most amenable events in the cohort were deep intronic, defined as more than twenty nucleotides from an exon, and not near the canonical sites.
entries.snippet: The majority (26/36, 72%) of the probably/possibly ASO-amenable mutational events were deep intronic, defined as being located more than 20 nucleotides away from an exon (Fig. 1b).

entries.proposition: NOT WWOX EVIDENCE. The experimental validation covered variants classed probably or possibly amenable; the unlikely class is not stated to have been tested.
entries.snippet: For two probably ASO-amenable variants (c.7865C>T, c.5763-1050A>G), patient fibroblasts were available for RNA-seq; for nine additional probably/possibly ASO-amenable variants, gDNA samples were available
